title: Schematicity under a finite locally free cover open in an affine scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $p:U\to X$ a representable surjective morphism from a scheme. Suppose every pullback of $p$ to a scheme is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; surjectivity means surjectivity of the field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $U$ is isomorphic to an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] of an affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $X$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. The open $U$ need not be quasi-compact, and no Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $S$ or $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07S6, proposition-finite-flat-equivalence-global, applied to the kernel-pair relation of p; paragraph immediately following the proof: locally closed subschemes of affine schemes satisfy condition (3).

proof.text: Form the scheme $R=U\times_XU$: representability of $p$ gives it by the scheme test $U\to X$. On each test $H$, its points are exactly pairs $(a,b)\in U(H)^2$ with $p(a)=p(b)$. The diagonal $a\mapsto(a,a)$, exchange $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$, and composition $((a,b),(b,c))\mapsto(a,c)$ define the kernel-pair groupoid; the groupoid identities are identities of ordered pairs. The projections $s,t:R\to U$ are finite locally free since each is the scheme pullback of $p$ along $U\to X$. Thus $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, and are surjective because of their diagonal section.

source.place: Tag 07S6 (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence-global), kernel-pair application; pairwise construction from the definitions.

proof.text: The singleton $\{p\}$ is fppf in the space sense: flatness and local finite presentation hold on every scheme test by hypothesis, and joint surjectivity is the assumed surjectivity on point classes. The fppf covering calculus, parts (2) and (4), shows that for each $a\in X(T)$ the represented pullback $P=T\times_XU\to T$ is an fppf covering of schemes. Its tautological map to $U$ lifts $a$. Consequently $X$ is the fppf sheaf quotient of $U$ by $R$: a map from the pointwise quotient into any fppf sheaf $G$ is an $R$-invariant map $h_U\to G$; evaluate it on these local lifts and glue in $G$. On overlaps the lifts are an $R$-point, so the evaluations agree. A common covering refinement proves independence of lifts, and uniqueness follows from the sheaf uniqueness axiom. This is precisely the universal property of sheafification, giving $X\simeq (U/R)^{\#}$.

source.place: Tag 07S6 (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence-global), quotient sheaf; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 03Y9 (lemma-fppf), base change; sheafification universal property.

proof.text: Identify $U$ with its given open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For $u\in U$, the orbit $E=t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$ is a finite nonempty set: $s$ has finite fibres and its section puts $u$ in $E$. For each $v\in E$ choose $f_v\in A$ with $v\in D(f_v)\subseteq U$ by the principal-open basis. Let $J=(f_v:v\in E)$. For every prime $\mathfrak p_v$ corresponding to a point of $E$, $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_v$, since $f_v\notin\mathfrak p_v$. Prime avoidance gives $f\in J$ lying in none of these finitely many primes. Hence $E\subseteq D(f)$. Every prime containing all $f_v$ contains $f$, so $D(f)\subseteq\bigcup_{v\in E}D(f_v)\subseteq U$. The principal open $D(f)$ is affine. Thus every orbit is contained in an affine open of $U$, without requiring a finite cover of $U$.

source.place: Paragraph after Tag 07S6: condition (3) follows from Properties Tag 01ZY (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine), case (2); direct open-in-affine argument using Algebra Tag 00DS (lemma-silly).

proof.text: Apply the invariant-affine lemma to each orbit from step 3. Obtain an affine open $W_u\subseteq U$ containing that orbit and satisfying $s^{-1}(W_u)=t^{-1}(W_u)$. The $W_u$ cover $U$, since $u$ belongs to its own orbit. Put $R_u=s^{-1}(W_u)=t^{-1}(W_u)$. The restricted relation on $W_u$ is exactly $R_u=W_u\times_XW_u$: if one endpoint is in $W_u$, invariance puts the other there. Also $R_u=U\times_XW_u$, so $R_u\to W_u$ is finite locally free by the scheme-test hypothesis on $p$; the other projection has the same property after exchanging endpoints. Since a finite morphism has affine inverse images of affine opens, $R_u$ is affine. The restricted relation is still an equivalence relation on every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 07S6 proof, first sentence; Groupoids Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine).

proof.text: Write $W_u=\operatorname{Spec}A_u$, $R_u=\operatorname{Spec}B_u$. The affine quotient theorem applied to $R_u\rightrightarrows W_u$ gives the affine $S$-scheme $M_u=\operatorname{Spec}C_u$, where $C_u$ is the equalizer of the two ring maps $A_u\rightrightarrows B_u$. It represents the fppf quotient $W_u/R_u$, with finite locally free surjection $W_u\to M_u$ and relation $R_u\simeq W_u\times_{M_u}W_u$. The map $W_u\to X$ is invariant, so the quotient universal property gives the induced map $h_{M_u}\to X\simeq(U/R)^{\#}$.

source.place: Tag 07S6 proof: apply Groupoids Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence) to each invariant affine open.

proof.text: The inclusion $W_u\to U$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and therefore flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the finding-opens lemma to the equivalence relation $R\rightrightarrows U$ and this inclusion. Its hypotheses on $s,t$ were checked in step 1. Its restricted relation is $R_u$ by step 4. With the quotient identifications in steps 2 and 5, its conclusion says exactly that $h_{M_u}\to X$ is representable by open immersions. In particular it is a monomorphism, so identify $h_{M_u}$ with its image subfunctor of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07S6 proof: Spaces Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), in the general flat locally finitely presented form of the cited node.

proof.text: For any $a:h_T\to X$, let $V_u\subseteq T$ be the open representing $h_T\times_Xh_{M_u}$. Pull back along the fppf covering $P=T\times_XU\to T$ of step 2, and let $b:P\to U$ be the lift. The opens $b^{-1}(W_u)$ cover $P$. On each such open $a$ factors through $W_u\to M_u\to X$, so it lies in the inverse image of $V_u$. Surjectivity of $P\to T$ therefore implies $T=\bigcup_uV_u$. This verifies Zariski coverage on every scheme test, rather than merely sheaf-local coverage. Since $X$ is an fppf sheaf it is a Zariski sheaf: open coverings are fppf, as open immersions are etale, hence flat and locally finitely presented. The representable open subfunctors $h_{M_u}$ now satisfy every hypothesis of the schemes representability criterion. It yields an $S$-scheme representing $X$. The index set is $|U|$, a set in the chosen site universes; for $U=\varnothing$, surjectivity makes $X$ empty and the empty family gives the empty scheme.
